At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program. After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one. VI – SEMESTER RULES
1. Dates/week of sessional exams and the final exam are announced at the commencement of the semester. Students are not allowed to miss any of the sessional and/or the final exams. No credit for the missed exams would be given to the student. 2. Students are allowed to apply online for the retake of any missed exam due to hospitalization, accident, or family emergencies such as the death or marriage of a blood relative. They must provide valid proof for any of these reasons. Please note that a mere medical certificate will not be accepted for this facility. 3. Students are strongly advised to avoid scheduling any personal events during the examination period. However, in case of a clash with an event, the committee may review the request based on submitted evidence and decide accordingly. 4. Please note that clashes due to Umrah or Itikaf will not be considered, as these are not mandatory requirements. 5. In all cases, the Director is the final authority who would, after consultation with the concerned faculty member (s), give a decision within one week from the date of submission of the application. 6. Students are allowed to Add/Drop a course during the first two weeks of the commencement of the semester. However, students admitted in First semester shall not be allowed to Add/Drop a course. Students are advised to attend all the classes of courses they intend to take during the semester. No add/drop requests will be entertained after the last date. 7. Students who have missed classes due to any unavoidable reason are to immediately (within two days) inform the Academic Office. Assignments, Quizzes, Presentations etc. missed (if any) should also be specified. No late applications for absence from classes shall be entertained. 8. It is the responsibility of the student to check his/her weekly attendance in the registered courses and to immediately report the Academic Office of any discrepancies. Submission of late applications will not be entertained. 9. Semester assignment, quiz, project, sessional grades are regularly upgraded and maintained by the respective course TA/Instructor and are available online. It is the responsibility of the student to check his/her grades and report any discrepancy to the Academic Office. Grades will not be changed if the student fails to report a grading discrepancy in an appropriate span of time.

context.section: Repeating a Course
context.text:
Repeating a Course
A student can repeat a course if that course has not been passed or the student desires to improve his/her grade. A student must repeat all failed courses. Students under warning must repeat such passed courses, in which their GPA is less than the minimum CGPA required for their degree. For example, MS students under warning (CGPA less than 2.50) must repeat courses in which their GPA is less than 2.50 (i.e. C or C- grade).

Description of Grades
The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester. SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester. CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts. The following points need to be noted: "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade. "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade “I” shall automatically convert to an “F” grade before the end of the next semester.
